title: Location transfer review
focus: Mix neutral-vowel choices, inessive forms, and complete location statements.

exercises.explanation: All three vowels in pöytä, ö, y and ä, belong to the front-vowel group.

optionFeedback.back vowels: Back vowels are a, o, u. The dots distinguish ä and ö from a and o; pöytä has front vowels.
optionFeedback.front vowels: Correct. Ö, y and ä are all front vowels.
optionFeedback.only neutral vowels: Only e and i are neutral. Pöytä contains ö, y and ä, which are front vowels.

exercises.misconceptionCategory: Vowel harmony: form not yet correct

exercises.explanation: Keep the stem kirjasto unchanged. Its a and o select the back-vowel ending -ssa: kirjastossa (“in the library”). The neutral i does not change that choice.

answerDiagnostics.explanation: The a and o determine harmony even though i is neutral. Use -ssa: kirjastossa.

exercises.explanation: Keep the stem myymälä unchanged. Its y and ä select the front-vowel ending -ssä: myymälässä (“in the shop”).

answerDiagnostics.explanation: Myymälä has front vowels y and ä. Use -ssä, preserving the dots: myymälässä.

exercises.prompt: Choose the harmonic ending. Which inessive ending belongs with museo (“museum”)?
exercises.explanation: museo (“museum”) takes -ssa because o is a back vowel. Neutral e and i do not force a back-vowel ending.

optionFeedback.-ssa: Correct. museo (“museum”) takes -ssa because o is a back vowel. Neutral e and i do not force a back-vowel ending.

exercises.prompt: Write “in the sauna.” Use sauna (“sauna”); The stem remains sauna; choose -ssa and attach it directly.
exercises.explanation: sauna (“sauna”) takes -ssa. Attach it directly to the unchanged stem: saunassa (“in the sauna”).

exercises.prompt: Write “in the forest.” Use metsä (“forest”); The stem remains metsä; choose -ssä and attach it directly.
exercises.explanation: metsä (“forest”) takes -ssä. Attach it directly to the unchanged stem: metsässä (“in the forest”).

exercises.instruction: Translate the Finnish form into English.
exercises.explanation: toimisto (“office”) takes -ssa. Attach it directly to the unchanged stem: toimistossa (“in the office”).

exercises.instruction: Translate the Finnish form into English.
exercises.explanation: päivä (“day”) takes -ssä. Attach it directly to the unchanged stem: päivässä (“during the day”).

exercises.instruction: Put the words in subject–verb–place order.
exercises.prompt: Build “The mother is in the office.”
exercises.explanation: Äiti on toimistossa. means “The mother is in the office”. The subject is plural or supplied, on agrees with it, and toimistossa gives the supplied place or state.
exercises.misconceptionCategory: Inessive location sentences: form not yet correct

sentenceExplanation.translation: The mother is in the office.
sentenceExplanation.pattern: Subject (who or what) + olla verb + place or state

parts.role: Subject — names who or what the sentence is about.
Verb — connects the subject to its place or state.
parts.formation: on is the supplied written form of olla for this subject.

parts.role: Place or state — completes the idea.
parts.formation: Start with toimisto and attach the learned inessive ending to form toimistossa.
